source.dataset: LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer Level-4 polar temperature maps (UCLA Diviner team, J.-P. Williams)
references: Williams, J.-P. et al. (2019) Seasonal polar temperatures on the Moon, JGR Planets 124, 2505-2521, doi:10.1029/2019JE006028
Schorghofer, N. & Williams, J.-P. (2020) Mapping of ice storage processes on the Moon with time-dependent temperatures, PSJ 1, 54, doi:10.3847/PSJ/abb6ff
source.doi_note: PDS dataset DOI resolves to LRO-L-DLRE-4-RDR-V1.0 (Diviner RDR). The binned polar cumulative tables behind these maps are in PDS4 bundle urn:nasa:pds:lro_diviner_derived1, collection data_derived_pcp (https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/urn-nasa-pds-lro_diviner_derived1/data_derived_pcp/). The gridded min/avg/max maps used here are the team's derived maps distributed by UCLA (https://luna1.diviner.ucla.edu/~jpierre/diviner/level4_polar/), not separately PDS-archived.

source.product_version: Williams+2019 maps: Diviner nadir RDR 2009-07-05..2019-02-17, GeoTIFF export 2023-02-07 (grids created 2019-11-04); 24x6 Tmean/Tmax: RDR 2009-07-05..2020-03-15, grids 2021-11-13; PDS PCP labels: PRODUCT_VERSION_ID 1, calibration software 4.0
source.resolution: 240.036 m/pixel (polar stereographic, true scale at the pole), 2533x2533 grid, 80-90 S
source.projection: South polar stereographic on a sphere R=1737.4 km, latitude of origin -90, central meridian 0, scale factor 1 at pole, false E/N 0; x = 2R tan(pi/4+lat/2) sin(lon), y = 2R tan(pi/4+lat/2) cos(lon); GeoTIFF PixelIsArea, UL corner (-304005.54 m, +304005.54 m); planetocentric lat, east lon
source.units: Kelvin (float32), no scaling factor; nodata = NaN (GeoTIFF GDAL_NODATA 'nan', netCDF NaN)

annual_mean.format: GMT netCDF-3 classic grid (x, y pixel centres normalised by R=1737.4 km)

method: Lat/lon converted to south polar stereographic x,y with the products' own documented projection (sphere 1737.4 km, k0=1 at pole). GeoTIFF row = floor((ymax - y)/240.036), col = floor((x - xmin)/240.036); for the netCDF .grd maps the pixel is located by its own x/y centre arrays (y stored south-to-north, flipped). Centre pixel = pixel containing the point; a 5x5 window (1.2 x 1.2 km) is read around it. Values are bolometric brightness temperatures (Diviner channels 3-9), no scaling. Annual min/max combine the Williams+2019 summer and winter min/max maps; annual mean is the Schorghofer & Williams 2020 Tmean map. All values are point/pixel measurements on a 240 m grid; diurnal/seasonal averages, not a single epoch.

orientation_test_shackleton.criterion: only the documented convention puts a cold (<110 K max) 5x5 window on the Shackleton floor

shackleton_floor.criterion: all layers < 110 K (permanently shadowed crater floor)

malapert_vs_published.published: ~180 K summer, ~130 K winter (Wueller et al. 2025 citing Williams et al. 2019)
malapert_vs_published.interpretation: The centre-pixel summer average (~155 K) is ~25 K below the quoted ~180 K, while the winter average (~145 K) is ~15 K above ~130 K. This is NOT a georeferencing error: the authors' own ASCII tables give the identical temperatures for this pixel and place its centre (clat/clon) within 0.1 m of ours, the Shackleton floor is cold only under the documented orientation, and zonal means show the season labels are right. The summit sits on a ridge crest with very steep temperature gradients (5x5 window: summer avg 137-167 K, winter avg 90-171 K); the pole-facing flank 0.5-1 km away is ~165-177 K in summer and ~90 K in winter; over a ~10 km box the summer-avg 90th percentile is ~181 K and the winter-avg median ~129 K. The quoted 180/130 K are therefore most likely rounded massif-scale / sun-facing-slope values rather than the value of the single 240 m summit pixel. The full text of Wueller et al. 2025 (doi:10.1029/2025JE009127) could not be retrieved (HTTP 403) to confirm which statistic/area they quote.

ridge_point_on_pixel_centre.criterion: NTRS 20240009936 says its ridge point was chosen to match LRO seasonal temperature data; if our grid is right, the point falls on one of our pixel centres (< 1 m)

ascii_table_crosscheck.description: Same pixel looked up (HTTP range requests) in the authors' ASCII tables, which carry their own pixel-centre clon/clat; tbol must equal the GeoTIFF value and the authors' pixel centre must equal ours. 'pass' covers the pixels that were looked up; 'not_checked' lists those that could not be (server not reachable).
